newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Agricultural Bank seeks buyers.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Agricultural Bank seeks buyers.

text.p: Bulgaria's troubled Bank for Agricultural Credit (BAC) needs to find a foreign buyer to avoid closure, executive director Yonka Kinova said on Monday.

"The central bank is expected to decide in the next few days on the future of the bank. The decision may be to close the bank if there is no investor interest," Kinova told an extraordinary meeting of shareholders.
"We plan to discuss with the Agricultural Bank of Greece a $10 million participation in our bank's projected capital rise," said Kinova.
In March, the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) acquired for free a 51.93 percent stake in BAC, which was previously held by BAC's owner businessman Atanas Tilev and his group of companies.
Withdrawal of some three billion levs by depositors at the beginning of the year caused a severe liquidity crisis in the bank.
In March, Tilev attributed the panic to a campaign by a group of companies close to the ruling Socialists which were being sued by BAC for failing to service loans of some $10 million.
Sixty five percent of the loans extended by the bank were considered unrecoverable, said head of BNB Bank Supervision Department Andrei Nikolov.
BAC hoped to raise its 500 million lev capital through transformation of 8.5 billion levs of central bank refinancing into equity.
The bank's capital to risk assets ratio is minus 23 percent.
The bank posted third quarter balance profit of eight billion levs. The bank lacks provisions of 22 billion levs.
The shareholders decided to free from responsibility the supervisory and executive boards for the May-September period. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
